reformulation: runs/test51-nomf-B1: the 2,480-var / 4,926-row MPS (5 simplex weights, 25 thresholds, 1,225 binary-controlled score pairs; 25 groups x 49 four-row blocks, epsilon=1/10000, all tied minima selected) becomes output/reformulated.mps (NAME test51r) with 159 vars / 289 rows / 1,773 nonzeros; 2,321 variables and 4,637 rows are gone and 288 surviving rows are substituted or M-tightened, so 93.6% of columns and 94.1% of rows are deleted. cases/test51 proves it with 3 directional claims (forward integer projection, reverse integer, reverse LP) at objective Equal: proof.rpa 6,045,374 B, proof.rpx 3,981,506 B, request.json 4,853 B, work 1,132,641, obligations 22,314, branches 1,874, linear_terms 219,494, peak_live_facts 13,748, verify execute 1.25 s, prepare 10.74 s.
claim_class: Objective-preserving exact integer-feasible projection, both directions plus an LP-mode reverse: 3 claims (reverse false/true/true, input_integers true/true/false) each carrying a 159-pair coordinate projection and objective 'Equal', claims 0 and 1 paired through the inverse field and claim 2 unpaired; no LP equality or strictness, and the V7 bijection mechanism is not engaged (verify statistics bijections=0, injectivity_coordinates=0, points=0).
claims: request.json (4,853 B) is exactly 3 claim records: {reverse:false, input_integers:true, output_integers:true, objective:'Equal', projection:159 [source_coord,target_coord] pairs, inverse:1}; {reverse:true, integers:true, inverse:0}; {reverse:true, integers:false, inverse:null} - the reverse claims carry the transposed 159 pairs, and each reverse block's proof map then restates all 2,480 source coordinates (map identical in blocks 1 and 2).

What the contract cannot say: nothing in request.json, nor in the RPX Claim layout (docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:99-106), names the 2,321 deleted columns, 4,637 deleted rows, 288 modified rows, the 130 M coefficients or the 4 mandatory gap rows; those exist as block obligations and, before the proof, as the analyst's 955,791 B audit.json, read by raw key at tools/prepare_test51.py:74 (fixed_zero_binary_certificates) and :300 (mandatory_fixed_zero_gap_rows).

Block 0 (forward integer) map is 159 affine entries, one projection identity per target coordinate; its 3,348 checks end with the 2,321 per-deleted-column reconstruction identities - checks[868:3189] are 2,321 distinct Local refs to Lin Eq steps whose only term is -1 times that coordinate's defining fact - followed by 159 'Exact'.

Blocks 1 and 2 (reverse) carry 10,175 and 8,791 checks: bound derivations and integrality for all 2,480 source coordinates, one check per each of the 4,926 source rows (158 RowLower, 1 RowEq, the rest Local Lin or 'Exact'), the objective equality, the 159 forward projection identities, the 2,321 reconstructions, and the inverse composition for the paired integer claim.

The delivered prose lives in cases/test51/preparation.json 'claims' (there is no cases/test51/README.md): 'Complete integer feasible-set bijection by projection and unique affine reconstruction, preserving every feasible objective value, all surviving coordinate observations, and both full inverse identities ... Objective-preserving target-LP inclusion into the source LP is additionally proved; LP equality and strictness are not claimed.'
proof_encoding: RPA 2 text = 'RPA 2\n' + one compact JSON object with exactly two keys, claims (= request.json verbatim) and blocks (3, one per claim, same order); 6,045,374 B of proof for a 4,853 B contract, i.e. 1,246 proof bytes per contract byte and 271 B per obligation.

Whole-tree step census: Lin 33,181, Cases 1,874, EqPair 1,096 and nothing else - no lifts, points, bijections or flow steps. Block 0 has 13,212 tree steps (10,242 Lin, 1,874 Cases, 1,096 EqPair) with top level 8,814 = 7,457 Lin + 1,355 Cases + 2 EqPair; block 1 is 9,191 flat Lin; block 2 is 13,748 Lin whose first 9,191 entries are byte-identical to block 1's steps, so 1,445,610 B (24% of the file) is one duplicated prefix.

Block 0's 1,094 'Eq' Cases are one split per fixed-zero binary (expression and split both z, integer {VarInt:z}, Witness and Absurd branches); its 261 top-level 'Le' Cases are 130 conditional selected-minimum upper rows plus 131 selected_bound calls whose balanced subset splits carry an Int fact over the left half and nest inside branch step lists (proof depth 5, JSON depth 25).

Kernel receipts (cases/test51/preparation.json): obligations 22,314, work 1,132,641 of 1e9, linear_terms 219,494, substitution_terms 76,172, peak_live_facts 13,748 of 1e6, branches 1,874, bijections 0, points 0; assemble 0.28 s and verify execute 1.25 s; canonical source 87,036 us, target 9,529 us; assembly and verification deterministic across three runs.

Negative checks: four mutations (missing_simplex_premise, wrong_case_integrality, missing_exceptional_gap, missing_inverse) are assembled and verified to INVALID with exit 2; receipts are only {status,message} ('INVALID contradiction witness', 'INVALID non-tautological exact obligation; obligation 503', 'INVALID missing obligation'), and the mutated artifacts are deleted so only the recipe survives in the preparer.
agent_manual_work: Wrote an exact MPS reader (Fraction from decimal tokens, INTORG/INTEND markers, RHS and BOUNDS set validation, refusal of unsupported sections) and proved the partition by hand over all 4,926 rows and 2,480 variables: 5 weights summing to 1, 25 thresholds, 1,225 (z,y) blocks, group g = 49g..49g+48, four rows per block - verified rather than inferred from names.

Ran the exhaustive within-group dominance census in its own eval Python: 1,090 binaries with a witness whose five coordinate gaps are all >= eps, 4 with strictly positive minimum gap below eps (x443, x630, x668, x995), 1,120 weakly dominated, and it refused to fix the 26 zero-margin ties after exhibiting an exactly feasible vertex w=(1,0,0,0,0) where all 26 are active.

Derived the 130 tightened M coefficients as max over retained candidates and coordinates (bound maximum 0.1419530064, zero only for x98), verified both binary cases of every retained lower and upper row (268 checks), and kept the four sub-epsilon lower-gap rows c1783, c2534, c2687, c4002 with their 20 pair-coordinate inequalities.

Evaluated 107 deterministic simplex points (5 vertices, equal weights, an edge point, 100 seeded rational points) under the induced minimum/tie assignment - 89 feasible, 18 infeasible, original and artifact agreeing on feasibility and objective - plus an explicit small-gap rejection point, then wrote the target MPS with a self-made fixed-column writer and re-read it with an independent Decimal fixed-column reader that matched rows, RHS, senses, domains, objective and integer markers.

Hand-produced output/audit.json (955,791 B: removed_variables 2,321, removed_rows 4,637, modified_rows 288 with before/after row contents, eliminated_score_definitions 1,225, bigM 130, two SHA-256 hashes, 107 scenario records) and an 11,595 B report.md with the two-direction projection proof; run row 19 turns / 19 tool calls / 0 failures / 377.6 s, no framework member touched, 38,390 eval characters.

friction: The contract is 159 coordinate pairs; the proof's load-bearing content is 2,321 per-deleted-column identities plus 4,637 deleted rows, and neither the Claim layout nor request.json has a field for a deletion record - so the preparer's source of truth is an external hand-written 955,791 B audit.json read by raw key (:74, :300) whose schema exists only in the analyst's Python.

Witness selection is outside the kernel: the preparer reads hint['witness'] and only re-derives and asserts the margin (:76-79), so the policy that separates 1,090 deletable upper rows from 4 mandatory gap rows (:198-205) and from the 26 retained zero-margin ties is transcribed from the analyst's prose, with no rule API to consult.

Structure recovery is a fragile whole-model pattern match keyed on the row name 'c0' and on nine exact row shapes, guarded by census asserts (:36-63); any extra row, extra term or renamed simplex row aborts the preparer, and the identical code is reused verbatim for test52's 266 groups and 53,467 rows.

Blocks are self-contained and their step lists are copied by hand: block 2's first 9,191 steps are identical to block 1's 9,191 (1,445,610 B, 24% of the RPA is that duplicate), trivial obligations are the literal string 'Exact' 4,606 times, and fact custody is passed through ChainMap plus a shared counter.

Failure receipts are unattributed: all four mutations return only {status:'INVALID',message:'...'} with a bare 'obligation 503' inside one message and no claim/block/step/obligation location object, so the negative checks cannot say which rule broke beyond the preparer's own 'reason' text, and each mutation had to be built by positional JSON surgery.

notes: Verdict on the assignment question: the claim is a projection contract - three claims of 159 coordinate pairs, objective 'Equal', paired through the inverse field, 4,853 B total - while the kernel must justify an edit set thousands of records deep (2,321 columns, 4,637 rows, 288 modified rows, 130 M coefficients, 4 mandatory gap rows); nothing in the contract layout can name a deleted coordinate (docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:99-106), so the deletion list lives in the analyst's audit.json and the compiler-side type for it does not exist. What the preparer did 2,321 times is the per-deleted-column reconstruction identity: block 0 checks[868:3189] are 2,321 Lin Eq steps whose only term is -1 times that coordinate's defining fact (1,225 score substitutions, 1,094 EqPair zeros, one constant 1 for x98, one threshold substitution for x1232), and the same 2,321 coordinates are restated inside each reverse block's 2,480-entry map - which is why a 93.6% column deletion costs 6.0 MB of proof for a 4.7 KB contract (271 B per obligation, 1,246 proof bytes per contract byte). Cost picture for a preflight capability: work 1,132,641 of 1e9, peak live facts 13,748 of 1e6, 219,494 linear terms, and 24% of the RPA is one duplicated step prefix; the same 313-line preparer at test52's scale (26,871 vars, 12,190 fixings, 1,055 conditional bounds) emits 78,134,488 B, 29% of the documented 256 MiB text limit (docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:390), which is the budget argument for a compact batch representation instead of per-record obligations. There is no cases/test51/README.md and no verify.py in the run dir, so the analyst's mechanical checks (107 scenario points, independent fixed-column reader, row reconstruction from original blocks) survive only inside its eval cells and as audit.json fields.
